For one day every June, South Africa’s searing racial inequality seems to melt away at Comrades race

In the early morning dark, thousands of runners waited, jostling with anticipation. South Africa’s national anthem rang out. Then the haunting swell of Shosholoza, first sung by Zimbabwean migrant workers in South Africa’s goldmines. Finally, that unmistakable, spine-tingling piano: Chariots of Fire.

guardian.description:
Woman detained at airport after allegedly making racist remarks directed at workers unloading baggage, police say

Brazil’s federal police have detained a Spanish citizen in São Paulo’s international Guarulhos airport for racism, in the latest of a series of high-profile arrests of foreign tourists on similar grounds.

Assailant behind shooting that left three people dead wrote ‘incel’-like manifesto that was posted by a far-right outlet

Attack targeted former Chile ambassador Orlando Letelier and his US colleague Ronni Karpen Moffitt

guardian.description:
Investigators says one of two teenagers who allegedly opened fire on students at high school was regular player

Philippine authorities have temporarily blocked the online gaming app GoreBox days after a rare school shooting in the south-east Asian country killed three students and injured 20 others.

guardian.title: Dettol apologises after ‘toxic men’ advert sparks backlash in China
guardian.description:
British disinfectant brand withdraws advert about a man’s efforts to find a ‘clean and untouched’ woman

The British hygiene brand Dettol has apologised after an advertisement released in China, which it said was intended to criticise “toxic men”, was widely condemned on social media as offensive to women.

The five-minute advert for a multipurpose disinfectant, released across many online platforms at the end of May, features a man comparing his girlfriend with his former partner.

Written in 1947, Kiyoshi Tanimoto’s account of the horrors of the atomic bomb attack will be published in August and is being made into a film

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'The average British citizen has lost over £3,000 a year'
rfi.description: Ten years after the UK voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains deeply divisive, with supporters and critics still at odds over its political and economic legacy. As part of RFI’s series marking the 10th anniversary of the referendum, we spoke to politics and international relations professor John Barry, one of its staunchest opponents.

rfi.title: Seven European countries urge ‘immediate halt’ to Sudan violence
rfi.description: Seven European countries have called on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to immediately stop their assault on El-Obeid, a city in Sudan's North Kordofan state, warning of credible signs that a major offensive could be imminent as civilians face worsening shortages of food, water and fuel.

rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: Portugal delays handover of French mother accused of abandoning children
rfi.description: Portuguese authorities have refused to immediately extradite to France a 41-year-old woman suspected of abandoning her two young children, who were found last month crying at the side of a road south of Lisbon.

rfi.title: Ghana dig in for stalemate with England at World Cup
rfi.description: Ghana fought their way to a 0-0 draw with England on Tuesday night that took them closer to qualifying for the knockout stages at the World Cup for the first time since their dazzling run to the last eight in 2010 in South Africa.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch was inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday in a sombre ceremony, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the country’s most symbolic events.

rfi.title: French government begins disciplinary action over child abuse case failings
rfi.description: The French government has announced disciplinary action against a magistrate and two gendarmerie officers over the handling of a suspect in child abuse case, which has lead to public outcry. This comes on the heels of a report which pointed to serious failings of the justice system, particularly with regards to minors.

rfi.title: Kenya halts US Ebola facility, health minister apologises for disobeying orders
rfi.description: Kenya has ordered a halt to preparations for a controversial US-run Ebola quarantine facility, the health minister told a court Tuesday, after being held in contempt for ignoring a previous stop-work order. The project has prompted widespread anger, and several people were killed during protests earlier this month.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

rfi.title: Messi notches up World Cup goals record to take Argentina into knockout stages
rfi.description: Argentina skipper Lionel Messi added another accolade to his otherworldly list of achievements on Monday when he became the record goalscorer at World Cups since the inception of the tournament in 1930

rfi.title: Haaland scores twice as Norway outwit Senegal to reach last 32 at World Cup
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice on Monday night as Norway advanced to the knockout stages at the World Cup following a pulsating 3-2 victory over Senegal in New Jersey.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

euronews.title: Catholics walk barefoot in mud ritual
euronews.description: Devotees in rice paddies cover themselves in mud and banana leaves for the Taong Putik festival, honouring St. John the Baptist with barefoot processions.

euronews.title: Scientists find human DNA over 2,000 years old in caves in Spain and Portugal
euronews.description: A research team based in Cáceres has found human DNA more than 2,000 years old on cave walls in Spain and Portugal, a discovery that could transform the study of prehistory.

euronews.title: Has Brexit made Europe stronger or weaker? MEPs go face-to-face on The Ring
euronews.description: What has Brexit taught Europe about sovereignty, migration, economic competitiveness, democratic accountability, and disinformation? Has it strengthened the case for deeper European integration? MEPs debate the future of EU-UK relations on this edition of The Ring.

euronews.title: UK records hottest June day ever as Europe swelters in heatwave
euronews.description: The Met Office has warned that "exceptionally warm" temperatures are expected to continue through the middle of the week.

euronews.title: Europe's five largest military powers meet ahead of key NATO summit with Ukraine in mind
euronews.description: The leaders of Europe's largest military powers met in Berlin on Wednesday in preparation for a pivotal NATO summit next month, to discuss support and security guarantees for Ukraine and how to strengthen the Atlantic Alliance's European Pillar.

euronews.title: German authorities carry out raids over alleged Russian gas sabotage
euronews.description: An investigation is looking into the sale of Gazprom's Berlin-based subsidiary Gazprom Germania, which took place around a month after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

euronews.title: Special Report: Brexit, ten years on: could the UK ever rejoin the EU?
euronews.description: Today's Special Report is anchored by Mared Gwyn and features correspondents Maria Tadeo and Shona Murray, alongside top interview guests, for a deep dive into one of the most consequential political decisions in modern European history: Brexit and the United Kingdom's departure from the EU.

euronews.title: IMF to closely monitor China’s economic growth amid trade tensions
euronews.description: An accurate measurement of China's digital economy is a priority for other powers competing with Beijing in fast-developing technologies.

euronews.title: London's Met police to scale up use of drones and live facial recognition
euronews.description: UK civil liberties campaign group Big Brother Watch has criticised the use of technologies such as drones and facial recognition.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | June 24th, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this June 24th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Portugal's World Cup victory sparks celebrations in Lisbon
euronews.description: Thousands of fans in Lisbon celebrated Portugal's 5-0 World Cup victory over Uzbekistan, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring twice and becoming the first player to score in six different World Cup tournaments.

euronews.title: Paris's Cirque d'Hiver begins renovation to restore its original splendour
euronews.description: Twenty ornamental frescoes from the Second Empire are to be restored over twelve to eighteen months. The seating, the polychrome ceiling canvas and the stained-glass windows will also be refurbished.

euronews.title: First whales killed as Iceland restarts commercial hunt
euronews.description: Iceland resumes commercial whaling after a two-year pause, with two fin whales processed at the Hvalur facility, reigniting controversy and protests.

euronews.title: Two workers for a Norwegian demining charity killed in Russian strike on Ukraine
euronews.description: The NPA has more than 450 staff based in Ukraine, where it has been carrying out mine clearance activities since 2023.

euronews.title: Heat records tumble: Spain breaks two June records
euronews.description: Spain's state meteorological agency, Aemet, reported that Monday and Tuesday were the hottest June days on record in mainland Spain since at least 1950.

euronews.title: Madrid, Woody Allen's new cinematic muse
euronews.description: Woody Allen’s next film, set entirely in Madrid, will treat the city as a star. Filming begins in October, following in the footsteps of New York, Paris, Rome and Barcelona.

euronews.title: EU proposes tax overhaul to cut business costs by €8 billion a year
euronews.description: The reform would reduce the compliance burden for businesses and facilitate cross-border payments.

euronews.title: European heatwave forces Eiffel Tower early closure and tourist attraction shutdowns
euronews.description: From the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre to Buckingham Palace's Changing of the Guard, soaring temperatures are forcing attractions to close, shorten opening hours and cancel events as a heatwave grips Europe.

lemonde.title: Après avoir enregistré sa journée la plus chaude, la France entraperçoit la fin de la canicule
lemonde.description: Avec une moyenne jour-nuit à 30 °C, ce 24 juin a établi un nouveau record de chaleur en France. Les prévisionnistes escomptent une sortie progressive de la canicule cette fin de semaine dans l’Ouest. La chaleur persistera jusqu’à mardi ou mercredi prochains dans le reste du pays.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : l’enquête visant Jérôme Barella élargie aux qualifications de meurtre et de viol sur mineur
lemonde.description: L’autopsie n’a pas permis de déterminer « avec certitude » la cause de la mort de l’enfant de 11 ans, a annoncé, mercredi 24 juin, le parquet d’Agen dans un communiqué.

lemonde.title: Les conclusions explosives des Assises du financement des universités : frais d’inscription multipliés par cinq, ouverture à la réduction du nombre d’étudiants…
lemonde.description: Le ministre de l’enseignement supérieur, Philippe Baptiste, souhaite qu’un débat s’ouvre sur ces sujets lors de la campagne présidentielle et estime qu’il « faut réfléchir à des mécanismes contributifs de la part des étudiants qui peuvent se le permettre ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Suisse-Canada : les deux sélections visent la première place, mais peinent grandement à se départager
lemonde.description: Pour la troisième et dernière journée du groupe B, la Suisse et le Canada s’affrontent pour obtenir la première place, tandis que la Bosnie-Herzégovine et le Qatar tenteront de poursuivre leur aventure à la Coupe du monde de football, mercredi, respectivement à Vancouver et Seattle.

lemonde.title: Patrick Weil : « Il n’y a pas de submersion migratoire »
lemonde.description: Avec « De l’immigration en France », le chercheur livre un essai pédagogique et vivace sur un sujet brûlant, à moins d’un an de l’élection présidentielle.

lemonde.title: Pedro Sanchez, gloire et douleur d’un des derniers dirigeants de gauche en Europe : « Agiter la peur d’un gouvernement d’extrême droite ne suffira pas »
lemonde.description: En incarnant l’opposition frontale aux politiques de Donald Trump et de Benyamin Nétanyahou, le dirigeant socialiste, à la tête de l’exécutif espagnol depuis 2018, s’est distingué sur la scène internationale. Une stature qui tranche avec le désaveu auquel il fait face dans son pays, alors que se multiplient les affaires visant son entourage.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le pays appelle à la vigilance quant aux « exercices de mobilisation » dans la région de Grodno, en Biélorussie
lemonde.description: « Du 20 juin au 2 juillet, le commissariat militaire du district d’Achmiany convoque environ 2 000 conscrits et met en place des points de rassemblement préliminaires », écrit le ministre des affaires étrangères ukrainien, Andrii Sybiha, sur le réseau social X. Ce district, faisant partie de l’oblast de Grodno, est frontalier de la Pologne.

lemonde.title: Cisjordanie occupée : un Palestinien tué lors d’un raid de l’armée israélienne à Al-Yamoun
lemonde.description: Un homme de 29 ans a été abattu mercredi lors d’une opération militaire dans le nord du territoire, selon le ministère de la santé palestinien et des témoins. L’armée israélienne a affirmé avoir visé un « terroriste ».

lemonde.title: La NASA s’apprête à lancer une mission de sauvetage risquée pour un satellite scientifique
lemonde.description: Le télescope spatial Swift, dont la réactivité est essentielle pour l’étude des sursauts gamma, est menacé par une hausse de l’activité du Soleil. Dans le cadre d’une mission mandatée par la NASA, un satellite a été mis au point pour partir à sa rescousse le 27 juin.

lemonde.title: Sébastien Lecornu promet un financement public pour la ligne à grande vitesse Bordeaux-Toulouse
lemonde.description: Le chef du gouvernement exclut un financement de la future liaison impliquant des acteurs privés. Une décision qui va à l’encontre des recommandations du Conseil d’orientation des infrastructures, auquel il avait confié le dossier en 2025.

lemonde.title: Au centre commercial Westfield Rosny 2, un début de soldes entre quête des bonnes affaires et recherche de fraîcheur
lemonde.description: Les soldes d’été ont démarré, mercredi 24 juin, en pleine canicule. Les commerces de centre-ville pourraient être délaissés au profit des grands centres climatisés, notamment ceux qui sont situés en périphérie.

lemonde.title: Les attaques ukrainiennes sur les raffineries russes provoquent des pénuries et… du mécontentement
lemonde.description: Depuis trois mois, les drones de Kiev visent en Russie raffineries, ports, dépôts, oléoducs. Avec des effets en chaîne sur l’économie russe. Dans les stations-service, l’essence se fait rare.

lemonde.title: Renault annonce 800 départs volontaires d’ici à 2027 parmi ses ingénieurs en France pour faire face à la concurrence chinoise
lemonde.description: Le constructeur a présenté aux partenaires sociaux une réorganisation de son pôle ingénierie, prévoyant une vague de départs volontaires essentiellement en Ile-de-France et le recrutement de 150 à 200 ingénieurs dans le logiciel et l’électrification.

lemonde.title: VIDEO Pedro Sanchez dément des accusations de corruption sous les rires de l’opposition
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre espagnol a démenti, le 24 juin, toute « corruption généralisée » de son gouvernement de gauche et du Parti socialiste ouvrier espagnol devant les députés.

lemonde.title: A Marseille, le marché du Soleil, haut lieu de la contrefaçon, devant la justice
lemonde.description: Quinze personnes sont jugées depuis lundi 22 juin pour avoir fait fonctionner ce grand bazar fréquenté par des clients en quête de bonnes affaires : les marchandises sont désormais pour l’essentiel contrefaites. Un dossier où la corruption est omniprésente.

lemonde.title: En Colombie, Ivan Cepeda reconnaît la victoire du candidat d’extrême droite, au terme du scrutin présidentielle le plus serré de l’histoire du pays
lemonde.description: Trois jours après un second tour décidé à moins d’un point d’écart, le candidat de gauche a accepté la victoire d’Abelardo de la Espriella, soutenu par Donald Trump. Son revers met fin à plusieurs jours de tensions et de heurts entre manifestants et police.

france24fr.title: Le clan Trump empêché en Albanie ?
france24fr.description: L’Albanie est dans la rue depuis plus de trois semaines. Les manifestants protestent contre la construction d’un complexe immobilier de luxe de Jared Kushner, le gendre de Donald Trump, et de sa femme Ivanka, dans une zone protégée où vivent de nombreux flamants roses. Le parquet anticorruption albanais a ouvert une enquête et cherche à comprendre comment ces terrains ont changé de mains et pourquoi leur valeur a explosé en quelques mois.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : la mine d'or de Mongbwalu reste active malgré la peur du virus
france24fr.description: À Mongbwalu dans le Nord-Est de la République démocratique du Congo, les chercheurs d'or continuent leur travail dans les mines malgré la peur du virus Ebola. L’épidémie Ebola qui a ressurgi dans l'Est du pays il y a maintenant plus d'un mois a déjà fait au moins 250 morts sur plus de 1000 cas recensés.

france24fr.title: Une canicule historique chaque année ?

spiegel.description: Aus einem Konflikt um Verkehrsberuhigung wird eine Standortdebatte: Der Tunnelbohrmaschinen-Pionier Martin Herrenknecht erwägt, einen Teil seines Unternehmens aus seiner Heimatgemeinde abzuziehen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 live: Schweiz gegen Kanada im Liveticker
spiegel.description: Im Gruppenfinale zwischen der Schweiz und Kanada reicht beiden ein Unentschieden für den Einzug in die K.-o.-Runde. Aber offenbar wollen sie lieber gewinnen. In Seattle führt Bosnien knapp gegen Katar. Der Livekommentar.

spiegel.title: Russland-Ukraine-Krieg: Sönke Neitzel über Putins Ziele und Europas Verantwortung - Spitzengespräch
spiegel.description: Sönke Neitzel sprach 2025 vom »letzten Sommer in Frieden«, heute ist er optimistischer. Doch im SPIEGEL-Talk mahnt der Militärhistoriker: Ohne mehr Ukrainehilfe und eine klare Europa-Strategie bleibt die Lage gefährlich.

spiegel.title: Vassili Golod übernimmt als Nachfolger von Georg Restle Leitung des ARD-Magazins »Monitor«
spiegel.description: Von Kyjiw nach Köln: Ukraine-Korrespondent Vassili Golod wird ab Frühjahr 2027 das ARD-Politikmagazin »Monitor« leiten.

spiegel.title: Social Media: Warum ein Verbot für Kinder und Jugendliche der falsche Weg ist
spiegel.description: Kinder vor den Gefahren der digitalen Welt zu schützen, ist eine der großen Aufgaben unserer Zeit. Warum Verbote wenig bringen – und die Schulen jetzt gefordert sind.

spiegel.title: »Ingeborg Bachmann – Jemand, der einmal ich war«: Geisterstunde einer stolz vereinsamten Dichterin
spiegel.description: Der Kinofilm »Ingeborg Bachmann – Jemand, der einmal ich war« mit Sandra Hüller mischt Spielszenen mit Doku-Aufnahmen der Schriftstellerin. Das ist eine riskante Dreistigkeit, gelingt aber eindringlich.

spiegel.title: Zohran Mamdani: New Yorker Bürgermeister baut seine Machtbasis in der Demokratischen Partei aus
spiegel.description: Bei den Vorwahlen in New York zeigt sich der junge Bürgermeister Zohran Mamdani als Königsmacher: Seine Kandidaten gewinnen gegen die des demokratischen Establishments. Strategen sprechen vom »Bürgerkrieg« innerhalb der Partei.

spiegel.title: Herne-Wanne: DHL-Bote wegen gefährlicher Körperverletzung verurteilt
spiegel.description: Ein DHL-Bote fühlt sich provoziert und prügelt auf zwei Menschen ein. Im Netz erfährt er dafür Verständnis, ein Video geht viral. Jetzt ist er verurteilt worden. Und der Richter gibt ihm einen Rat.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Hitze stellt neue U-Bahn ohne Klimaanlage auf die Probe
spiegel.description: Bei ihren neuen U-Bahnen verzichtete die Berliner Verkehrsgesellschaft auf Klimaanlagen – über 30 Grad werde das Thermometer schon nicht steigen. Der SPIEGEL machte den Hitzetest – das Ergebnis fiel eindeutig aus.

spiegel.title: Hitze in der Wohnung: Was Mieter vor dem Kauf einer Klimaanlage wissen müssen
spiegel.description: Um die 40 Grad am Wochenende: Wem Ventilatoren nicht ausreichen, der denkt womöglich über eine Klimaanlage für die Wohnung nach. Nicht nur Mieter müssen dabei einiges beachten. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Neun Polizisten schweigen nach tödlichem Polizeieinsatz
spiegel.description: In Mülheim an der Ruhr stirbt ein Mann in einem Krankenwagen, nachdem Polizisten ihn mit Kabelbindern gefesselt haben. An seinem Tod tragen die Beamten keine Schuld, sagt die Staatsanwaltschaft, dennoch seien sie zu weit gegangen.

spiegel.title: Hitze-News: Hitze sorgt für Absage des Halbmarathons in Hamburg am Sonntag
spiegel.description: Ein Lauf-Event in Norddeutschland muss kurzfristig verschoben werden. Spanien misst höchste Juni-Temperaturen seit mehr als 70 Jahren. Und: Die Hitzeprognose für Deutschland. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Bahn schafft Fritten im Bordbistro ab: Pommes Schranke? Das war einmal
spiegel.description: Erst das frisch gezapfte Bier, jetzt Pommes: Ohne Rücksicht auf die kulinarischen Vorlieben ihrer Gäste mistet die Deutsche Bahn ihr Angebot im Bordbistro aus. Ein Skandal? Im Gegenteil.

spiegel.title: Angela Merkel und das Porträt fürs Kanzleramt: Die Frau, die sich nicht traut
spiegel.description: Endlich! Angela Merkels Porträt für die Ahnengalerie des Kanzleramtes ist fertig und soll kommende Woche vorgestellt werden. So mutig, sich von einer Frau malen zu lassen, war sie allerdings nicht.

spiegel.title: Fußball: Maja Göthberg erhält nach Vertragsstopp bei Lazio Rom Schadensersatz
spiegel.description: Maja Göthberg und Lazio Rom hatten sich schon auf einen neuen Vertrag verständigt, dann war das Angebot plötzlich vom Tisch. Nun fällte der Internationale Sportgerichtshof ein Urteil, das schwangere Spielerinnen schützt.

spiegel.title: Andy Burnham, Favorit für die Starmer-Nachfolge in Großbritannien: Der freche Junge aus Manchester
spiegel.description: Keir Starmers instinktlose Politik hat die Labour-Partei in eine schwere Krise geführt. Sein möglicher Nachfolger Andy Burnham hat gezeigt, dass er Nigel Farages rechtspopulistische Partei Reform UK schlagen kann. Wer ist der Mann?

spiegel.title: Streit zwischen Polen und der Ukraine: »Chaos, multipliziert mit Hysterie«
spiegel.description: Präsident Selenskyj reist nicht zu einer Ukrainekonferenz nach Danzig, die Beziehung zu Polen ist auf einem Tiefpunkt. Der ukrainische Historiker Jaroslaw Hrytsak warnt, der Streit gefährde den europäischen Erweiterungsprozess.

observador.title: Luís Neves rejeita falha no caso das ameaças a Montenegro
observador.description: Luís Neves diz que não houve "falha de coordenação" no caso do MAL, mas admite que nem tudo foi partilhado com a UCAT. Lista de alvos só foi descoberta no fim da investigação.

observador.title: PS trava corte com PSD e aposta na estratégia do desgaste
observador.description: PS quer adiar a decisão sobre o Orçamento, evitar ser visto como detonador de uma crise e gerir o risco de um avanço da direita. Prefere expor o Chega na oposição e esperar por desgaste do Governo.

observador.title: 9.º Ano. Rey da Matemática pede transparência na avaliação
observador.description: O influencer e professor de Matemática divulgou prova nas redes sociais pelo segundo ano consecutivo. Garante que não pediu nada aos alunos e defende "recriação pedagógica" dos exercícios.

observador.title: Kremlin condena o ultimato de Zelensky a Lukashenko
observador.description: Zelensky deu uma semana a Minsk para desmantelar sistemas russos de retransmissão de sinais na Bielorrússia. Kremlin considera uma escalada agressiva e uma interferência na soberania bielorrussa.

observador.title: Rússia avalia proibição total de exportações de gasóleo
observador.description: O objetivo é estabilizar o mercado interno de combustíveis face à crescente escassez e ao aumento dos preços, ligados aos ataques de drones ucranianos a refinarias de petróleo e redes de distribuição.

observador.title: Rubio avisa Irão: portagens em Ormuz "não vão acontecer"
observador.description: Durante uma visita ao Kuweit, Marco Rubio sublinhou que "o mundo inteiro opõe-se", incluindo os países da região, à cobrança de portagens ao tráfego marítimo no estreito de Ormuz.

observador.title: Ex-jogador do Gil Vicente suspeito de assalto em Palma
observador.description: Madou Camara, de 20 anos, terá sido um de três envolvidos no assalto a um homem de 80 anos em Palma. O jogador foi apontado como ainda pertencente aos quadros do Gil Vicente, mas clube já veio negar.

observador.title: Diogo Sousa ruma a França por 11 milhões de euros
observador.description: Formado no clube desde os oito anos, o médio fez 28 jogos na época de estreia na equipa principal e ajudou a conquistar a Taça da Liga.

observador.title: 20h. Mundial. Começa hoje a última jornada da fase de grupos
observador.description: Do grupo B, Suíça e Canadá decidem o primeiro lugar. Bósnia e Catar tentam pontos para continuar em prova. E o PS diz que acordo alcançado com o Governo da PSU foi feito com foco nos mais vulneráveis.

observador.title: Brilhantes Dias sobre PSD: "Há sempre caminho"
observador.description: Líder parlamentar do PS admite novo capítulo na relação entre partidos e recusa “guerra de semântica” com o Governo na PSU sobre trabalho social, após sugerir queda da obrigatoriedade.

observador.title: Elites pressionam Netanyahu a travar ações na Cisjordânia
observador.description: A missiva, dirigida a vários membros do governo israelita, foi assinada por dois ex-primeiros-ministros, vários antigos chefes de segurança, um prémio Nobel e o mais reconhecido romancista do país.

observador.title: Estrela. PCP acusa Moedas de ignorar obra ilegal
observador.description: João Ferreira diz ter “todas as evidências” de ilegalidade nas obras que transformaram o quiosque num restaurante de luxo. Câmara não apresenta projeto de alterações nem autorização.

observador.title: "Irão nunca ganhou uma guerra, mas nunca perdeu negociação"
observador.description: João Albuquerque, especialista em Relações Internacionais, destaca a forma como Israel move "linhas vermelhas" a seu gosto, tratando os apelos de paz dos EUA como meras sugestões.

observador.title: Portugal é um dos criadores de plataforma pelo numerário
observador.description: A nova plataforma pretende intervir no debate europeu sobre o futuro dos pagamentos, defendendo a coexistência entre meios digitais e numerário num sistema considerado mais equilibrado.

observador.title: 19h. PSD nega que trabalho social seja facultativo na PSU
observador.description: Hugo Soares diz que é uma questão de retórica. Já o PS recusa entrar em guerras de semântica. Ainda, o MAI garante que não vão existir grandes filas de espera nos Aeroportos, durante o verão.

observador.title: "O calor não é só o tempo, é uma emergência de saúde"
observador.description: Segundo a OMS, o calor provocou mais de 200 mil mortes na Europa apenas nos últimos quatro anos. A organização alerta que a mortalidade associada ao calor aumentou cerca de 30% nos últimos 20 anos.

observador.title: Como a tecnologia moldou a bola do Mundial
observador.description: A bola do Mundial é uma ferramenta essencial que transforma o futebol em arte. Em 2026, esse papel coube à Trionda, uma bola que funde a tecnologia com a aerodinâmica para revolucionar o jogo.

observador.title: Metro de Lisboa. Presidente não prevê "oposição" a horário
observador.description: O esclarecimento de Cristina Vaz Tomé sobre o projeto piloto do alargamento do horário do Metro de Lisboa para as 5:00.

nyt.description: The first housing package in decades will take time to put into effect, testing the patience of families rankled by high prices.

nyt.description: The anti-establishment left surged. How shaken are party leaders?

nyt.description: More than a dozen countries have issued urgent heat warnings. France saw its highest average temperature ever on Tuesday.

nyt.description: The burning of fossil fuels is raising temperatures worldwide, but local factors, on land and at sea, determine which regions warm most rapidly.

nyt.description: After weeks of speculation over Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding plans, a permit has been filed for an event at Madison Square Garden over the July 4 weekend.

nyt.description: Sentiment is shifting amid frustration in the antiabortion movement that more abortions are happening now than when Roe v. Wade fell.

nyt.description: An unlikely trio of justices issued a slashing critique of plea bargains that included several references to orangutans.

nyt.description: Cash might be a relic, but — like royalty and emperors — President Trump still wants his face on American currency.

nyt.description: The searches, by police internal affairs investigators and federal authorities, stemmed from earlier scrutiny of Jeffrey Maddrey, the former chief of the department, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

nyt.title: Frank Carone, Longtime Eric Adams Associate, Is Arrested in Bribery Scheme
nyt.description: Brooklyn federal prosecutors accuse Mr. Carone and his brother of profiting from the city’s migrant crisis. He was the chief of staff to former Mayor Eric Adams.

republika.description: L’Oms dichiara “l’emergenza sanitaria”, il ministro Schillaci convoca una riunione per l’emergenza. Due i morti nei campi agricoli. Il picco nella Penisola è atteso per il weekend

npr.title: Greetings from sweltering Switzerland
npr.description: On the waterfront in Lucerne, Switzerland, soccer fans watched jumbo TVs showing a World Cup match played an ocean away. But the air felt more like the tropics.

npr.title: U.N. nuclear chief says inspectors will visit Iran, but Iran says only after final deal
npr.description: The head of the U.N.'s atomic agency said Iran's nuclear enrichment sites would be inspected as part of the interim deal. Iran insists any such visit would only come after a final deal.

npr.title: Inside the gold-mining town where the Ebola outbreak likely started
npr.description: NPR reports from Mongbwalu in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The fight to contain the virus faces obstacles from lack of supplies to residents who doubt that the virus is real.

npr.title: As U.S. government looks to leverage food aid, producers seek other delivery methods
npr.description: The U.S. is changing the way food aid is distributed to starving children around the world. It is now using aid as a diplomatic tool as nutrition bars pile up in U.S. factories.

npr.title: Archaeologists find huge Viking textile production site in Denmark
npr.description: Archaeologists have discovered a huge Viking Age textile production site in Denmark that dates back more than 1,000 years and underlines the sophistication of Viking society.

npr.title: Afghan Taliban hold first, closed-door talks with EU on deportations
npr.description: Rights groups criticized the meeting, saying it undermines the EU's human rights obligations.

npr.title: U.S. lifts Iran oil sanctions. And, federal judge rules SAVE voter tool unlawful
npr.description: The U.S. has temporarily lifted oil sanctions on Iran as peace talks continue. And, a federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's data system, known as SAVE, is unlawful.

npr.title: Who would pay for Trump's proposed $300 billion Iran reconstruction fund?
npr.description: It's still unclear who would fund a proposed $300 billion reconstruction plan for Iran. Former National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan called the whole approach "something entirely new."

npr.title: A U.S.-Iran dispute over nuclear inspections clouds work to finalize a war-ending deal
npr.description: As U.S.-Iran talks continued, a break in the shipping bottleneck through the Strait of Hormuz appeared to be in the works.

npr.title: Lebanese struggle to get by in an ancient city under Israeli evacuation order
npr.description: In one of the oldest cities in Lebanon, once besieged by Alexander the Great, ordinary people struggle to survive Israeli attacks.

new-sci.description: We have developed genetic technologies that could wipe out entire species of pests that are harmful to us. Columnist Michael Le Page says the flesh-eating screwworm is the most likely first target

new-sci.title: You should turn off fans when it's too hot – but how hot is too hot?
new-sci.description: Fans can make you hotter rather than cooler, but the temperature at which you should turn them off depends on several factors, including your age and the humidity level

new-sci.title: Huge crater in Australia may be the oldest impact structure on Earth

new-sci.title: Elite Maya people had teeth placed in a cave far from their tombs
new-sci.description: A cave in Belize contains teeth from dozens of important Maya people buried elsewhere, which may attest to a ritual intended to ensure their passage to the underworld

new-sci.title: Parenting may permanently improve brain health for mums and dads

new-sci.title: SpaceX's secretive plans to deliver cargo to Earth from space

new-sci.title: How some people's brains make an extraordinary recovery from stroke
new-sci.description: Around a third of people are able to almost fully rebuild their brains after a stroke and uncovering why is pointing the way to better treatments for everyone

new-sci.title: Unapproved gene therapy for boosting longevity is set to go on sale
new-sci.description: A gene therapy that instructs cells to produce more of an anti-ageing protein called klotho is about to be offered by a US company at overseas clinics to bypass FDA rules

new-sci.title: Woman with Alzheimer's starts conversing again after taking psilocybin
new-sci.description: A woman with severe Alzheimer's disease who hadn't spoken more than monosyllables in years began initiating conversation after a single dose of psilocybin

new-sci.description: A spider living in the rainforests of Queensland, Australia, builds a snare trap reminiscent of a Roman-era ballista weapon that it uses to catapult green tree ants into a web 30 centimetres above

new-sci.title: How menopause radically changes the brain – and what happens after
new-sci.description: The brain undergoes a full renovation during menopause. Although these changes are profound, we’re learning that the long-term impact needn’t be all bad

new-sci.title: ‘Fusogenic’ neurosurgery let paralysed pigs walk again – are we next?
new-sci.description: Researchers say a surgery that let pigs with completely severed spinal cords walk again may lead to human trials, and then perhaps even full head or brain transplants. Columnist Helen Thomson is intrigued but sceptical of whether the technique can be successful in humans

new-sci.title: A promising natural technique to remove CO2 could backfire
new-sci.description: Several start-ups have tried to grow seaweed to remove atmospheric CO2, but this could affect the levels of nutrients in the ocean and hamper other CO2-sucking processes

phys-org.title: Are algorithms unfairly screening out immigrant job applications?
phys-org.description: Canada's new artificial intelligence strategy, AI for All, presents an ambitious vision for the country's future. Artificial intelligence, the federal government argues, can boost productivity, strengthen competitiveness and create opportunity across the economy.

phys-org.title: Preserving wooden heritage in the Arctic as thaw, rot and tourism converge
phys-org.description: Historic wooden structures across Svalbard are crumbling under the combined weight of climate change and human activity. Longer, warmer, and wetter seasons fuel wood-decaying fungi, while tourism adds physical wear to sites never built to last. The ArcticAlpineDecay project has provided a crucial baseline of knowledge—revealing how vulnerable these cultural landmarks are and why continued monitoring will be essential in the years ahead.

phys-org.title: Scientists design 'tunable' biomolecules to probe how sugars behave
phys-org.description: Sugars are not just a source of energy—they also play a crucial role in how cells communicate, how proteins interact and how materials behave in medicine and industry. But studying these processes is challenging because sugar molecules are structurally complex and difficult to control.

phys-org.title: How 'catchy' music is driven by rhythmic patterns
phys-org.description: Puerto Rican icon Bad Bunny, a superstar rapper, has recently risen to global prominence, as demonstrated by the 2026 Super Bowl halftime show.

phys-org.title: A new quantum computer sets a high watermark for accuracy. Are we on the verge of a big breakthrough?
phys-org.description: In a laboratory in Broomfield, Colorado, 98 atoms are suspended in midair, held in place by electric fields and cooled to temperatures close to absolute zero.

phys-org.description: A 100-year-old equation and a fiber-optic cable off the coast of Svalbard led researchers to discover they could detect swimming whales—even if they were completely silent. The discovery broadens the tools biologists could someday use to detect and monitor these marine giants.

phys-org.title: AI spots landslide risks near power towers before failures, tests show
phys-org.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) can identify landslides and other geological changes that threaten electricity transmission towers, potentially helping operators intervene before infrastructure fails, according to research in the International Journal of Power and Energy Conversion.

phys-org.title: Mathematicians unleash multifold speed boost for supercomputer simulations of molecules
phys-org.description: More than 20% of the workload on the world's 500 fastest supercomputers is spent simulating how atoms and molecules move—with applications ranging from material design to identifying drug interactions to understanding protein folding.

phys-org.title: Expert studies emergence of identity-based labor organizing
phys-org.description: In the post-COVID-19 era, worker unionization campaigns have increasingly been organized by groups who feel stung by virtue signaling from corporations espousing progressive values, especially those pertaining to LGBTQIA+ issues.

phys-org.title: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is treated with nanobubbles. What are they and how do they work?
phys-org.description: As the United States approaches its 250th birthday celebrations on July 4, Washington, DC's monuments, statues and fountains are being prepared to put on a show.

phys-org.title: Human DNA can survive on cave walls for thousands of years, opening new window into prehistory
phys-org.description: For the first time, scientists have shown that ancient human DNA can survive for thousands of years on cave walls, opening new ways to study prehistoric human activity. This interdisciplinary study was conducted within the framework of the First Art project, which is led by researchers from Spain and Portugal in collaboration with institutions across Spain, Portugal, the U.K., China and Germany.

phys-org.title: Heavy rain may be driving tire pollution into Florida waterways
phys-org.description: Florida International University scientists have, for the first time, detected a toxic tire-derived chemical in Florida waterways and developed a new testing method that makes it easier to find and monitor the pollutant at extremely low levels. The study focuses on 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a toxic chemical formed when the tire additive 6PPD reacts with ozone in the atmosphere. phys-org.title: Pop song lyrics grew more self-focused in the US and Germany over 50 years, research reveals
phys-org.description: Over five decades, popular songs in the U.S. and Germany have become more self-focused—as indicated by the use of pronouns such as "I," "me" and "mine"—while no such trend was seen for the most popular songs in Japan and Hong Kong. Marius Golubickis of United Arab Emirates University and colleagues present these findings in PLOS One.

phys-org.title: Sicily remained a medieval melting pot despite major political and religious upheavals, ancient DNA reveals
phys-org.description: Sicilian populations have been genetically diverse for many centuries, and they have remained that way even through major regime changes and religious transitions, according to a study published in PLOS One by Aurore Monnereau of the University of York, U.K., and colleagues.

phys-org.title: Decades-long dataset shows which orcas are most at home in Puget Sound
phys-org.description: Data spanning nearly half a century shows that endangered southern resident killer whales are spending less time in inland waters, whereas their larger cousins, Bigg's killer whales, are increasingly present in Puget Sound.

phys-org.title: Introducing Weather Jiu-Jitsu, a new approach to avert catastrophic weather events
phys-org.description: In a new perspective paper, Qin Huang of Arizona State University and colleagues propose that the worst damage from extreme weather events could be prevented through Weather Jiu-Jitsu, a theory-based approach to "nudge" weather systems away from harmful trajectories. The paper was published in PLOS Water.

phys-org.title: Machine learning rediscovers equations governing ocean biogeochemistry
phys-org.description: Climate and ocean models use a series of equations to represent complex natural processes. However, the equations used in these models are often derived from limited observations and a series of assumptions.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum.
